Ligand 1 carries a cyclopentyl on its amide nitrogen - atom 13 is that ring's CH, bonded to the nitrogen at atom 11 over a non-ring bond - and that anchor is what I need here, because it keeps a ring rather than a methyl and so leaves the azine substituent completely free to be anything. This is the live lead from the last run. The C4 halogen series reads fluorine 0.53, chlorine 0.50 to 0.53, bromine 0.60, and it had not converged when the budget ran out. Iodine is the next point: larger still, far more polarisable, and the weakest electron-withdrawer of the four, so if the series keeps climbing it settles that the position rewards polarisability rather than electronics. The cost is real - iodine takes the molecule to about 421 Da and will pull QED down to roughly 0.82 - so this probably will not win on Phi even if activity rises. I am using a cyclopentyl cap rather than my usual cyclopropyl simply because this host supplies it, and cap ring size measured activity-neutral three separate times, so it does not confound the reading.
